277: Illegal exaction claim: no payment by the plaintiff to the government, so the exaction claim fails.
No facts as alleged in the complaint concern the payment of money by Mr. Piszel; thus, Mr. Piszel's illegal exaction claim must also fail.
335: Implied-in-fact contract claim for interest on seized funds under the Tucker Act fails; claimant did not establish mutuality of intent.
Mr. Evans has not demonstrated an implied-in-fact contract with the Government for interest accrued on the seized funds.
377: Dismissal of the Fort Laramie Treaty 'bad men' money claim for failure to exhaust administrative remedies with the Department of the Interior.
Thus, the Claims Court properly dismissed his treaty claims for failure to exhaust administrative remedies.
433: Other Tucker Act money claims: no taking, breach of contract, or money-mandating statute alleged, so no Tucker Act jurisdiction
The appellants failed to allege any taking, any breach of contract, or any violation of a money-mandating statute or regulation as would be required for jurisdiction under the Tucker Act.
601: Other money claims: whether the government's liability for additional PILT payments under 31 U.S.C. § 6902 is limited to the amount Congress appropriated under § 6906 (2006), so the counties cannot recover the difference between full statutory formula amounts and actual payments for FY2006 and FY2007.
we conclude that the applicable version of § 6906 limits the government's liability under PILT to the amount appropriated by Congress.
767: Tucker Act money-mandating jurisdiction over breach of a mediation confidentiality provision; court held the agreement was not money-mandating and affirmed dismissal for lack of jurisdiction
Mr. Higbie fails to show that the mediation agreement involved in this dispute is money-mandating.
855: Other Tucker Act money claims: whether constitutional amendments, federal statutes and regulations cited by the claimant mandate compensation from the United States
Tucker Act jurisdiction is limited to claims against the United States based on sources of law that mandate monetary relief.
1023: Money-mandating source for a Tucker Act claim: 31 U.S.C. § 1321(a)(22) and DOJ Circular 2244 do not impose a specific fiduciary obligation enforceable by damages.
Neither § 1321(a)(22), (b)(1) nor DOJ Circular 2244 qualifies as such statutory or regulatory prescriptions.
1027: Implied contract claim for money damages based on RICO §1964(c) as a contract offer failed; no contract existed between plaintiffs and the government.
Plaintiffs' allegations do not establish that any contract existed between Plaintiffs and the government.
1318: Just compensation for a rails-to-trails taking: the appraisal of before-taking fair market value must account for physical remnants of the railway easement; court vacated and remanded the compensation award on the government's appeal.
We conclude that the fair market value of the land includes the physical remnants of the railway that would have remained on the landowners' property but for the issuance of the NITUs.
1334: Whether NAHASDA is money mandating so as to support Tucker Act jurisdiction over tribes' grant-formula claims; court held it is not money mandating.
NAHASDA does neither, as revealed by the ultimately equitable nature of the Tribe's claims.
1335: Whether alleged procedural failures in HUD grant decision resulted in an illegal exaction supporting jurisdiction; court rejected the illegal exaction theory because the claim concerns property never in claimant's possession.
An illegal exaction claim must be based on property taken from the claimant, not property left unawarded to the claimant, rendering the Tribes' exaction claim invalid on its face.
1345: Other money claims: whether the Fort Laramie Treaty 'Bad Men' clause supports a money claim, where the court held the plaintiff failed to exhaust administrative remedies under the treaty.
we conclude that he has not exhausted his administrative remedies under the Fort Laramie Treaty. We therefore affirm.
1563: Implied-in-fact contract claim for payment of an invoice against the government: plaintiff failed to show offer, acceptance and consideration.

As far as Mr. Taylor's breach of contract claim was concerned, the court explained that Mr. Taylor had failed to demonstrate the existence of the elements of offer and acceptance and valid consideration necessary for an implied-in-fact contract with the government.
1564: Illegal exaction claim: complaint failed to state an illegal exaction claim under Norman because the statute does not provide for a return of money unlawfully exacted.
the court held that Mr. Taylor's complaint failed to allege an illegal exaction claim.
1570: Whether Nyabwa's wrongful-conviction damages claim under 28 U.S.C. § 1495 can rest on vacated Texas state convictions; the court held that an 'offense against the United States' requires a federal offense and that immigration detention under federal deportation statutes does not qualify.
Because his vacated criminal convictions were the result of Texas state law, they do not suffice.
1581: Tucker Act jurisdiction over double jeopardy and Fourteenth Amendment section 4 constitutional claims, which are not money-mandating; court affirmed dismissal for lack of jurisdiction

Neither the double jeopardy clause of the Fifth Amendment nor section 4 of the Fourteenth Amendment mandates the payment of money by the government; therefore, neither claim falls within the waiver of the Tucker Act.
1582: Unjust conviction and imprisonment claim under 28 U.S.C. § 1495 dismissed; conviction was by Virginia, not the United States, and § 2513 allegations and certificate were absent
The court also committed no error in dismissing Mr. Taylor's claim of unjust conviction and imprisonment pursuant to 28 U.S.C. § 1495
1593: Other money claims: illegal exaction claim under §13(3) of the Federal Reserve Act based on the Government's acquisition of AIG equity; court vacated merits holding without reaching it
We therefore vacate the Claims Court's judgment that the Government committed an illegal exaction and remand with instructions to dismiss the equity-acquisition claims that seek direct relief.
1595: Other money claims: reverse stock split claims alleging the Government engineered the split to avoid a common shareholder vote; trial court's denial of relief affirmed under clear-error review
We agree with the Government that the trial court did not clearly err in finding that the reverse stock split was not a vehicle designed by the Government to obtain AIG common stock.
1889: Whether a claim under 28 U.S.C. § 1495 for unjust conviction succeeds where the plaintiff was convicted under state law and lacks a certificate of innocence or pardon.
Because Cochrun was convicted of violating the laws of South Dakota, and was not convicted of violating federal law, he cannot sue under § 1495.
2275: Other Tucker Act money claims: breach of enlistment contract for medical care and tort-based negligence and malpractice claims were not within Tucker Act jurisdiction.
To the extent they sound in tort, the Tucker Act does not cover them.
2441: Other money claims: the statutory double-wages penalty under 46 U.S.C. § 10504(c)(1) cannot be enforced against the government, so the claim for penalty payments fails.
We therefore conclude that Lagergren cannot enforce § 10504(c)(1) against the government.
2457: Constitutional claims (Fifth Amendment due process, Fourteenth Amendment equal protection, First Amendment) not within Tucker Act money-damages jurisdiction.
Accordingly, we affirm the Court of Federal Claims' decision to dismiss Hood's constitutional claims in Case Number 15-1200 and Case Number 15-1501.
2460: Tort claims (fraud and conspiracy) outside Tucker Act jurisdiction.
The Court of Federal Claims therefore correctly concluded that it lacked jurisdiction to consider Hood's allegations of fraud and conspiracy.
2478: Tucker Act money claim based on alleged unexecuted 'admiralty civil contracts'; plaintiff failed to identify a contract or substantive right to money damages against the United States.
Gullet-El failed to allege facts sufficient to establish that he entered into a contractual relationship with the United States.
2526: Whether the Title Deeds, Heavenly Laws, Ninth Amendment or other asserted sources are money-mandating under the Tucker Act; held not money-mandating.
Appellants have not identified any relevant source of law that is money-mandating against the United States.
2708: Scope of Indian treaty bad men provision (1868 Treaty art. 6): court holds only wrongs that could give rise to arrest and criminal prosecution are cognizable, so the CFC's criminal-wrong limit is upheld
We therefore hold that only wrongs that could give rise to arrest and potential criminal prosecution are cognizable under the 1868 Treaty's bad men provision.
2709: Geographic limit on bad men provision: CFC erred in holding off-reservation wrongs categorically non-cognizable; off-reservation acts that continue on-reservation wrongs may be cognizable and the CFC must assess them on remand
the geographic line is not as bright as that drawn by the CFC.
2710: Affirmative-acts limitation on bad men provision: court vacates the CFC ruling that alleged omissions are not cognizable and leaves them for remand
We therefore vacate the CFC's ruling that the alleged omissions are not cognizable under the bad men provision, and we include those omissions, to be addressed anew if necessary, in the remand.
3239: Count I: whether the Cobell settlement release bars the Fort Berthold breach-of-trust money claim (settlement treated as a contract and interpreted); government prevailed
We therefore affirm the Court of Federal Claims' grant of summary judgment.
3255: Breach of a negotiated settlement agreement (Tucker Act money claim): the Army did not breach by finding Baker unsuitable based on pending felony charges under 5 C.F.R. § 731.202, so the government was entitled to summary judgment.
3420: Other money claims: penalties claim dismissed for lack of a money-mandating source of substantive law under the Tucker Act.
Absent an affirmative money-mandating statute, the Claims Court did not have jurisdiction to adjudicate the damages claim.
3525: Unjust Conviction and Imprisonment Act damages: whether time served on the overturned firearm conviction is compensable where the same time was credited under 18 U.S.C. § 3585(b)(2) to a lawful sentence on another charge; court held no damages are owed.
we reverse the judgment below and hold that Mr. Crooker is not entitled to any damages under the Unjust Conviction and Imprisonment Act.
3609: Breach of settlement agreement: whether OPM breached paragraphs 6 and 7 by not consulting the Survey Implementation Committee and Technical Advisory Committee; held no breach.
we conclude that, under the circumstances, OPM was not required to consult the SIC or the TAC and, thus, did not breach the Settlement Agreement by failing to do so.
3610: Breach of settlement agreement: whether OPM breached paragraph 10.4.3 by failing to give class-member notice before departing from the Conforming Methodology; held adequate notice given.
OPM provided adequate notice to the class members by publishing the 2010 Interim Regulations in the Federal Register.
3611: Breach of implied and express covenants of good faith and fair dealing in eliminating COLA; held no breach.
Accordingly, OPM's acts did not violate the duty of good faith and fair dealing.
3707: Tucker Act implied-in-fact contract claim for pension benefits against the Government; court held no mutuality of intent and no privity, so claim fails
Because we determine no mutuality of intent exists, we do not reach the question of whether the other required elements of an implied-in-fact contract exist in this case.
3799: Illegal exaction claim from Treasury Offset Program: no genuine issue of material fact; government entitled to summary judgment because the debts were not shown to be discharged and no child support offset shown.
we instead remand for entry of summary judgment in favor of the government on that claim.
3803: Money claim under I.R.C. §§ 6212 and 6213 and tort and due process claims: no money-mandating source of law, so no Tucker Act claim
Nothing in either section provides a right to damages if the government fails to comply with the stated requirements.
3904: Tucker Act money-mandating requirement: plaintiff identified no substantive right to money damages against the United States, so the money claims fail.
Thus, in order to invoke jurisdiction under the Tucker Act, a plaintiff must point to a substantive right to money damages against the United States.
3945: Money claim for CERCLA clean-up costs under Avgas Contracts; damages amount and allocation, including reasonable certainty, stipulations, and allocation among plaintiffs, decided for the Oil Companies (claimants)
3954: Statutory claim under 42 U.S.C. § 1342 risk corridors payments: court held section 1342 created an obligation to pay the full statutory amount, but appropriations riders suspended that obligation for FY2015-2017, so the statutory claim fails.
we hold that the riders on the relevant appropriations effected a suspension of that obligation for each of the relevant years.
3955: Implied-in-fact contract claim: court held the risk corridors program did not create a contract promising full risk corridors payments, so Moda cannot state a contract claim.
Accordingly, Moda cannot state a contract claim.
3961: Other money claims: whether due process claims against the government are money-mandating under the Tucker Act, so the Claims Court could award money damages.
The Claims Court's jurisdiction, however, does not extend to claims under the Due Process clauses of the Fifth and Fourteenth Amendments because they are not money-mandating provisions.
4122: Money claim under the Tucker Act for cost-sharing reduction payments under the ACA; the court affirmed the Court of Federal Claims' judgment for the government by reference to Moda Health Plan and Land of Lincoln.

For the reasons stated in our decisions in Moda Health Plan, Inc. v. United States, 17-1994, and Land of Lincoln Mutual Health Insurance Co. v. United States, 17-1224, and consistent with the statement of appellant Maine Community Health Options, we affirm.
4197: Other money claims: whether the government owes ACA risk corridors payments to the health plan under the Tucker Act; the court affirmed the Court of Federal Claims judgment for the government by reference to Moda Health and Land of Lincoln.

For the reasons stated in our decisions in Moda Health Plan, Inc. v. United States, 17-1994, and Land of Lincoln Mutual Health Insurance Co. v. United States, 17-1224, and consistent with the statement of appellant Blue Cross and Blue Shield of North Carolina, we affirm.
4210: Tucker Act money-mandating status of ACA section 1402/18071(c)(3) cost-sharing reduction reimbursement provision; insurers may sue for damages in the Court of Federal Claims for unpaid reimbursements.
4268: Tucker Act/§7430 litigation cost award: whether BASR is a prevailing party under the qualified offer rule, including whether a partnership can be a party in a TEFRA proceeding, whether tax liability was in issue, whether costs were incurred, and whether the real-party-in-interest doctrine bars the award; the court affirmed the award for the claimant.
4269: Abuse of discretion review of the award of litigation costs under I.R.C. §7430 based on the $1.00 qualified offer being made in good faith; court held no abuse of discretion.
We therefore conclude that the trial court did not abuse its discretion.
4331: Other money claims: breach of contract claim and land patent claim against the United States rejected for failure to establish a contract or a money-mandating source of law.

The Claims Court also correctly dismissed Mr. Langan's breach of contract claim against the United States for lack of subject matter jurisdiction because Mr. Langan failed to plausibly establish the existence of an express or implied contract with the United States.
4435: Tribal trust money claim: whether the AFLEA and TFPA create a fiduciary duty to maintain sufficient security in the trust estate, and whether the claim states a claim for damages.

Thus, the AFLEA, in combination with the TFPA, "defines a fiduciary relationship" by providing that the Government was to "hold in trust" security, at a level adequate to secure Collier's payment obligations, for the benefit of ITCA and the Navajo Nation.
4437: Whether the Government had a concurrent fiduciary duty to negotiate adequate security terms in the TFPA; the court found no support for such a duty.

ITCA did not cite, and we have not found, support in the AFLEA, case law, or otherwise, for the proposition that the Government's fiduciary duty to "hold in trust" the security against Collier's payment obligations, imposes a concurrent duty on the Government to "negotiate terms in the TFPA and related documents to ensure adequate security"
4455: Other Tucker Act money claim: recovery of withheld reimbursement payments for allowable costs under the cooperative agreement.
Accordingly, the Court of Federal Claims erred in concluding the State's use of the SAM formula to calculate fringe benefits was improper under the Agreement.
4459: Just compensation for taking of kish and scrap: whether the trial court was obligated to fashion its own damages award when the claimant's evidence was insufficient; zero damages affirmed.

We hold that the trial court in a takings case is not obligated to fashion its own award when a plaintiff has not provided evidence sufficient to determine just compensation with reasonable certainty.
4619: Illegal exaction claim over issuance and maintenance fees and other alleged damages; court held no plausible illegal exaction because the PTO collected fees within its statutory authority.
The PTO did not collect fees in excess of its statutory authority, and therefore did not illegally exact those fees.
4762: Debt Collection Act offset and inherent government right to recover erroneously paid appropriated funds: the court held the United States has an independent right to recover overpayments of U.S. Funds and may offset them under the DCA.
This is because the United States has an independent and inherent right to recover erroneously expended congressionally appropriated funds.
4763: Whether the government actually overpaid Agility under the PCO contract: the CFC erred by treating the overpayment determination as conclusive, so the merits must be reviewed on remand.
Thus, we vacate the decision of the Court of Federal Claims granting judgment in favor of the government.
4766: Whether the government complied with the procedural protections of 31 U.S.C. § 3716(a) before offsetting; material factual dispute precludes judgment for the government.
Whether Agility received the required DCA procedures is a material factual dispute which should have precluded judgment in favor of the United States.
4781: Breach of the implied duty of good faith and fair dealing in a 2007 settlement agreement; the Federal Circuit held the implied duty could not impose security and non-discrimination obligations untethered to express terms, so the damages judgment on this theory could not stand.

Because the Claims Court's judgment was not based on the government undermining any specific promise of the 2007 agreement, we conclude that the judgment for breach of the covenant of good faith and fair dealing cannot be sustained.
4782: Express breach of paragraph 10 (comply with 'all laws') of the 2007 settlement agreement; the court held 'all laws' does not include ATF internal orders, so no express breach was shown.
We agree with the Claims Court's conclusion that the express language of the 2007 agreement does not admit of Dobyns' construction of "all laws."
4983: Lump-sum payment under the LSPA (5 U.S.C. 5551) excludes evening and weekend additional pay under 38 U.S.C. 7453(i); government's money-claim position upheld against the claimants' claim for additional pay in lump-sum payments.

In sum, the plain language of 38 U.S.C. §7453(i) compels the conclusion that Appellants are not entitled to have evening and weekend "additional pay" included in their lump-sum payments under the LSPA.
4984: Entitlement to pre-judgment interest under the Back Pay Act on lump-sum payments for accrued annual leave; no express waiver of sovereign immunity for interest, so the government prevails.
We hold that the Court of Federal Claims did not err in ruling that Appellants are not entitled to pre-judgment interest on the lump-sum payments they received for accrued and unused leave.
4998: Tucker Act money claim based on federal Indian trust responsibility: no statute or regulation identified that creates trust obligations or money-damages entitlement, so the claim fails.
Ms. Cloud identifies no statute or regulation that gives rise to trust obligations that were allegedly violated here.
5008: Constitutional and statutory money claims (Fourth, Sixth, Eighth, Thirteenth, Fifteenth Amendments, Due Process, Civil Rights Act, Speedy Trial Act, DOMA, UCMJ) not money-mandating
From what we can decipher, none of Maxberry's constitutional or statutory claims are moneymandating or otherwise confer jurisdiction in the Claims Court.
5059: Other Tucker Act money claims: Count I (takings and due process claim based on a district judge's rulings) and Counts II-III (Copyright Act and RICO claims against non-government parties) were not within Tucker Act money-damages jurisdiction.

Jurisdiction of the Claims Court is established by the Tucker Act, which contains no provision extending jurisdiction of that court to any individual or organization other than the United States—or to any claims other than for liquidated or unliquidated damages.
5215: PSOB death benefits claims: whether Louisiana insurance fraud investigators were 'law enforcement officers' under the PSOBA and 28 C.F.R. § 32.3, so benefits were properly denied; includes rejection of deference to the Louisiana statute and Chevron deference to the regulation's definition. Affirmed denial for the government.

The BJA Director's Determinations were therefore not arbitrary or capricious, and were supported by substantial evidence because none of Jeansonne and Sledge’s duties fell under the categories set out in 28 C.F.R. § 32.3.
5346: Other money claims: application of Florida centerline presumption to determine landowners' ownership of corridor land abutting plats, resolved on summary judgment in landowners' favor by reversal.
We conclude, for those reasons, that the trial court erroneously granted summary judgment in its original ruling as to the land at issue on appeal.
5553: Tax gross-up as part of contract damages (Tucker Act money claim): whether the Court of Federal Claims' tax gross-up award was supported by a fair and reasonable approximation of future tax consequences, given income held constant from a single tax year

Because the Court of Federal Claims clearly erred in using income from a single tax year to predict the future rates at which each partner would pay taxes, we vacate the tax gross-up award and remand for entry of judgment consistent with this opinion.
5558: Amount of a Section 1603 ARRA cash grant: whether Treasury may reduce the cost basis of qualified property in proportion to its use in producing electricity, so that the grant covers only the electricity-related share of cost. Court held the statute allows the reduction, affirming the government's grant amount.

we conclude that Section 1603(b)(2)(A) unambiguously allows Treasury, in calculating the amount of the grant specified in the statute, to reduce the basis of qualified property in proportion to its use in a qualifying activity.
5569: Tucker Act breach-of-settlement claim: whether the 1985 settlement agreement obligated the government to guarantee future annuity payments after the insurer's liquidation; held no such obligation, so the government prevailed.
Because the Shaws' agreement did not obligate the government to act as a guarantor of the future periodic annuity payments, we affirm the Claims Court's grant of summary judgment to the government.
5655: Other money claims: fraudulent tax collection claim is a tort outside Tucker Act jurisdiction
But a claim of fraudulent tax collection is essentially a tort claim.
5656: Fourth Amendment claim does not mandate compensation and is outside Court of Federal Claims jurisdiction
Therefore, Ms. Pekrul's Fourth Amendment claim is outside the jurisdiction of the Court of Federal Claims.
5818: Section 1603 ARRA cash grant amount: whether Treasury may reduce the cost basis of qualified property in proportion to its use in producing electricity, so that the grant is limited to 30 percent of the allocable cost.

we conclude that Section 1603(b)(2)(A) unambiguously allows Treasury, in calculating the amount of the grant specified in the statute, to reduce the basis of qualified property in proportion to its use in a qualifying activity.
5910: Illegal exaction claim based on DOE offset requests barred by issue preclusion from prior district court judgment; dismissal sustained on the merits.
As to this claim, we sustain the dismissal on the merits rather than the lack of jurisdiction.
5929: Section 1603 ARRA cash grant amount: claimants failed to prove the agreement-stated development fees reliably measured actual development costs and were properly excluded from the grant cost basis; government's sham/unreliable-fee position upheld, and judgment for the government affirmed.
We read the Court of Federal Claims opinion as finding that the amounts stated in the development agreements do not reliably indicate the development costs. That finding is not clearly erroneous.
6037: Statutory liability under ACA section 1402 for unpaid cost-sharing reduction reimbursements (Tucker Act money claim); court affirmed liability for claimants.
In these cases, following our decision in Sanford, we affirm the Claims Court's decisions as to liability.
6038: Damages for 2017 cost-sharing reductions: government's request for a damages offset rejected; award affirmed.
Here, as in Sanford, we see no basis for a 2017 damages offset and affirm the Claims Court's award of 2017 damages.
6039: Damages for 2018 cost-sharing reductions: government entitled to offset damages by additional premium tax credits received as a direct result of insurers' mitigation (with insurers bearing the burden of persuasion on the amount); reversed and remanded on damages.

We conclude that additional premium tax credits were received by Community and Maine Community in 2018 as a direct consequence of their mitigation efforts following the government's nonpayment of 2018 cost-sharing reduction reimbursements, and the Claims Court was required to credit the government with such tax credit payments in determining damages.
6146: Section 1603 grant basis: whether I.R.C. § 1060 residual method applies to the Alta transactions (goodwill or going concern value could attach), so the purchase price must be allocated using the residual method.

we conclude that goodwill and going concern value could have attached to the group of assets transferred in the Alta transactions immediately after the transaction and that those assets constitute a "trade or business"
6170: Statutory and contract claims for risk corridors payments under the Affordable Care Act, decided by reference to the companion Moda Health Plan decision; the claims fail.
For the reasons stated in our decision in the companion case, Moda Health Plan, Inc. v. United States, No. 17-1994, the statutory and contract claims of appellant Land of Lincoln mutual health fail.
6314: Merits of the illegal exaction claim: interpretation of 28 U.S.C. § 1913 note limiting PACER fees to expenses of providing public access to federal court electronic docketing information, with government liable for certain expenditures (Mississippi Study, VCCA Notification, E-Juror, most Courtroom Technology) and not for CM/ECF and EBN.
We therefore hold that § 1913 Note limits PACER fees to the amount needed to cover expenses incurred in services providing public access to federal court electronic docketing information.
6666: Other money claims: Treaty of 1855, Indian Civil Rights Act, and the 1891 Act do not supply money-mandating or contract-based Tucker Act jurisdiction; 1891 Act bars claims for depredations after its passage.
the Claims Court correctly determined that the 1891 Act prohibits claims based on depredations occurring after passage of the Act.
6718: Illegal tax collection claim is essentially a tort claim outside Tucker Act jurisdiction under 28 U.S.C. § 1491.
But a claim of fraudulent tax collection is essentially a tort claim.
6750: Other money claims: implied-contract claim based on paying court filing fees, and constitutional/due process and separation-of-powers money claims, held not money-mandating under the Tucker Act.
But the mere filing of a complaint and payment of a filing fee does not create a contract between the plaintiff and the United States.
6786: Breach of section 515 loan prepayment contracts: court held Saline did not place the government in breach before selling the properties, so no breach of contract occurred.
We conclude that the CFC correctly denied Saline's claim for breach of contract.
6812: Illegal exaction claim for wharfage and tonnage fees collected by Customs from 2008 to 2011; the court held Customs was authorized under 48 U.S.C. 1469c and the 1994 MOA, and that the authority was not revoked by VIPA's 2007 letter or the 2006 tariff amendment.

Because Customs was authorized under 48 U.S.C. § 1469c, in combination with the 1994 MOA, to collect the disputed fees from February 2008 to March 1, 2011, and because that authority was not revoked during that time, we affirm the Claims Court's grant of the United States' motion for summary judgment.
6994: Recovery of allegedly unlawful M&R payments under CVPIA §3407(d); whether the proportionality requirement is a 'limitation' that takes priority over the $50 million collection target, so the Bureau's assessments were unlawful.
We disagree with the court's interpretation of the statute, and we therefore reverse and remand for further proceedings consistent with this opinion.
7017: Tucker Act money claim for full debt relief under the Pigford consent decree; court held the decree did not provide the claimed remedy and the 2005 reexamination decision was unreviewable.
Slaughter's claim that he was entitled to full debt relief was not a remedy provided for by the consent decree.
7036: Enforcement of the class settlement agreement against the Government; Government's claim that the parties abandoned the agreement rejected as unsupported by mutual, unequivocal conduct.
The Court of Federal Claims did not clearly err in finding no mutual intent to abandon the Settlement Agreement
7067: Unjust imprisonment damages claim under 28 U.S.C. § 2513: no jurisdiction because Burmaster was never convicted and submitted no certificate or pardon of innocence.
For these reasons, the Claims Court correctly dismissed Burmaster's claim for lack of jurisdiction.
7284: Whether the settlement agreement's finality clause barred a suit for breach of the agreement; the court held it did not and the claim may proceed.

We see no basis for construing the finality provision in the Agreement to bar suit for breach of the Agreement, and we conclude that the Claims Court erred in determining that the Agreement precluded Mr. LaBatte's suit for breach of contract.
7505: Other Tucker Act money claims: contract, unjust conviction (28 U.S.C. §§ 1495, 2513), treaty, and due process/other amendment claims were not within money-mandating jurisdiction against the government.
The Court of Federal Claims does not have jurisdiction over a due process violation because this clause is not a money-mandating source.
8007: Other Tucker Act money claims: whether sequestration applies to reduce Direct Payment Build America Bonds payments under the ARRA; statutory claim dismissed because sequestration applies

we agree that sequestration applies to Direct Payment BABs because these payments are issued from the permanent, indefinite appropriation provided by 31 U.S.C. § 1324, which constitutes direct spending.
8064: Barrett's derivative illegal exaction claim, premised on the net worth sweep exceeding FHFA's statutory authority, fails under Collins
Collins makes clear that Barrett cannot plausibly allege an illegal exaction claim predicated on his contention that adopting the net worth sweep fell outside the FHFA's statutory authority.
8576: Other money claims (due process, Fourth Amendment and tort-type conversion claims) found not money-mandating under the Tucker Act
the Due Process clauses of both the Fifth and Fourteenth Amendments do not mandate the payment of money and thus do not provide a cause of action under the Tucker Act.
8662: Tucker Act money claim: Kelly's claim to a share of recovered federal funds failed because she was neither in privity with the United States nor a third-party beneficiary of the Annual Contribution Contract between HUD and the Omaha Housing Authority.

Nothing in that stated purpose indicates an intent on the part of the contracting parties (the United States and the City of Omaha) to benefit Ms. Kelly, as required to state a claim as a third-party beneficiary.
8664: Other money claims: whether Tucker Act or other statutes confer jurisdiction over claims for declaratory, injunctive or tax-lien-related relief against the IRS; court held no other statute confers power to grant relief
We also conclude that Mr. Bishay has not identified any other statute that confers power on the Claims Court to grant his desired relief.
8799: Existence of an implied-in-fact nonexclusive copyright license permitting the Navy's copying of BS Contact Geo; court affirmed the Claims Court's finding that the license existed, which favors the government.
we affirm the Claims Court's finding of an implied-in-fact license between the Navy and Bitmanagement.
8800: Whether the express contracts between the Navy and Planet 9 and between Planet 9 and Bitmanagement precluded the implied-in-fact license; court declined to apply the preclusion rule.
For these reasons, we decline to apply the preclusion rule on this record.
8801: Navy's failure to comply with the Flexera condition of the implied license made its copying outside the license scope and thus copyright infringement; judgment for government vacated and remanded.
the Navy's failure to abide by the Flexera condition of that license renders its copying of the program copyright infringement.
8802: Measure of 28 U.S.C. § 1498(b) damages on remand (statutory damages, hypothetical negotiation, Navy's burden of proving usage); addressed in footnote and challenged by Judge Newman as not briefed or decided below.

If Bitmanagement chooses not to pursue statutory damages, the proper measure of damages shall be determined by the Navy's actual usage of BS Contact Geo in excess of the limited usage contemplated by the parties' implied license.
8931: Tucker Act money claim: no money-mandating statute (10 U.S.C. provisions cited) and no express or implied contract was shown, so the damages claim failed.
None of these statutes can be fairly interpreted as mandating compensation by the government for what Mr. Starrett alleges.
8952: Illegal exaction claim: no exaction because Columbus had only a contingent interest and no vested property interest in the recovered funds; dismissal affirmed.
We therefore affirm the court's dismissal of Columbus's illegal exaction claim under Rule 12(b)(6).
9006: Section 1603 ARRA grant: whether a specified energy facility must achieve ideal or near-ideal production levels to be placed in service (statutory and regulatory interpretation of placed-in-service). Court held no such requirement, against claimants.
We agree with the trial court's decision and the Fifth Circuit's Sealy opinion: to be placed in service, a facility need not achieve ideal or near-ideal production levels.
9007: Section 1603 grant: the facilities' specifically assigned function is to produce and sell electricity, not baseload production under the PPAs or environmental compliance; clear-error review of the Court of Federal Claims' finding, against claimants.

The Court of Federal Claims did not clearly err in rejecting Appellants' arguments or finding that the facilities' specifically assigned function is to produce and sell electricity, so we affirm its finding.
9008: Section 1603 grant: placed-in-service date under the five-factor test (permits, critical testing, daily operation); clear-error review found all five factors indicate placed in service in 2008, against claimants.
Therefore, the Court of Federal Claims did not clearly err in finding that all five factors indicate that the facilities were placed in service in 2008.
9115: Other Tucker Act money claims: Fourteenth Amendment, Bill of Rights, Thirteenth Amendment and HUD-form contract theories rejected as not money-mandating or not creating a contract with the government.

That the Department of Housing and Urban Development created mortgage forms and oversees some aspects of mortgages does not make it a party to the mortgage and does not provide jurisdiction in the Court of Federal Claims.
9142: Illegal exaction claim based on wage garnishment of a federal debt; the court held the government did not collect the debt in contravention of any statute, regulation, or other authority, including the notice and garnishment-notice challenges.
Mr. Horton's illegal exaction claim accordingly fails as a matter of law and summary judgment denying this claim was properly granted.
9177: Government's right to offset ACA reinsurance debts against risk-adjustment debts during state insolvency: no statutory offset under Colorado law, no equitable common-law offset, and no federal common-law offset right beyond that of an ordinary creditor.

we hold that Colo. Rev. Stat. § 10-3-529(1) provides an offset right that is limited to contractual obligations. Because the obligations here arise out of a statute, § 10-3-529 does not afford the government a right to offset.
9179: Whether the Tucker Act provisions (28 U.S.C. §§ 1503, 2508) or 31 U.S.C. § 3728 bar the Claims Court from entering a money judgment for the claimant despite the government's asserted offset; court held the money judgment proper.
But § 3728 does not prevent the Claims Court from entering judgment.
9214: Tucker Act money-mandating source for tribal/trust fund claims: the 1906 Act establishes a money-mandating fiduciary duty to distribute royalties to individual headright owners, so the Claims Court erred in finding no money-mandating source.

Because the Claims Court did not recognize that the 1906 Act establishes a trust relationship between the government and the headright owners, it erred in finding that plaintiffs failed to specify a source of substantive law that establishes a money-mandating trust relationship.
9265: Illegal exaction claim: garnishment of Social Security benefits to collect a valid VHA debt is not an illegal exaction, so the money claim fails on the merits.
The existence of Mr. Peamon's valid debt to a government agency, the VHA, means the garnishment of his Social Security benefit payments is not an illegal exaction.
9625: Other Tucker Act money claim under the Clean Water Act §1323: whether Wilmington's stormwater fees were reasonable service charges, so that the United States waived sovereign immunity for them. The court held the fees were not a fair approximation and not reasonable service charges.

As a result, the fees Wilmington charged the USACE are not "reasonable service charges" as defined by 33 U.S.C. § 1323(c), and the CWA does not waive the USACE's sovereign immunity with respect to those charges.
9675: Illegal exaction claim (Tucker Act money claim) predicated on unlawful conservatorship; dismissed for failure to state a claim.
an illegal exaction claim predicated on the alleged unlawfulness of the agency action is not plausible as a matter of law.
9875: Equal Pay Act prima facie case under 29 U.S.C. 206(d); court overruled Yant's added requirement that the pay differential be based on sex and vacated the Rule 12(b)(6) dismissal, so the EPA claim proceeds. Coded as other money claim (pay claim against government).

To make out a prima facie EPA case, a claimant bears the burden to "show that an employer pays different wages to employees of opposite sexes 'for equal work on jobs the performance of which requires equal skill, effort, and responsibility, and which are performed under similar working conditions.'"
10057: Other Tucker Act money claim: whether submission of whistleblower Form 211 created an enforceable implied or express contract with the IRS supporting breach of contract damages
The Court of Federal Claims correctly held that the submission of a whistleblower Application Form 211 does not create a contract-based obligation enforceable in that court.
10340: Other money claims: treaty-based (1866 Cherokee Treaty art. 9) and trust-based claims for damages under the Tucker Act were held not money-mandating.
As the Claims Court held, however, that statement is not fairly interpreted as "mandating compensation by the Federal Government."
10371: PSOB Act payee eligibility under 34 U.S.C. 10281(a)(4)(A): Goodrich not eligible as payee because the Illinois designation form did not expressly, specifically, or unmistakably refer to PSOB benefits under 28 C.F.R. 32.13.
Therefore, we cannot plausibly read the Illinois Form to encompass a designation of PSOB benefits.
10372: PSOB Act payee eligibility under 34 U.S.C. 10281(a)(4)(B): Goodrich not eligible because no life insurance policy was on file with the public safety agency; the court rejected the regulation's substantial-equivalent argument and intent evidence.
Accordingly, Ms. Goodrich cannot qualify for PSOB benefits under the plain language of § 10281(a)(4)(B).
10446: Implied contract money claim (Tucker Act) found insubstantial and futile; no non-frivolous allegation of contract with the government
We agree with the court (Appx. 22–23) that Mr. Greene's motion failed to describe "a non-frivolous allegation of a contract with the government,"
10542: Unjust conviction claim under 28 U.S.C. § 1495 fails because the plaintiff never obtained the certificate of innocence required by 28 U.S.C. § 2513, so he cannot prove the necessary facts.
We agree with the Court of Federal Claims that Mr. Brewer's claim for monetary relief under § 1495 cannot succeed without him having been granted a certificate of innocence.
10620: Tucker Act money-mandating jurisdiction: whether NWPA §10156(e) impact assistance provision is money-mandating for the county's claim; court held not money-mandating, so no Tucker Act jurisdiction
We conclude, therefore, that the Claims Court lacked jurisdiction under the Tucker Act to hear Butte County's claim.
10657: Other Tucker Act money claim: whether the United States is liable for nonpayment of FEGLI insurance proceeds under 5 U.S.C. § 8705(e) and the OPM regulations; claim held not cognizable against the government.
We conclude that the United States has not waived its sovereign immunity for claims seeking insurance proceeds.
10891: Other money claim (PSOB death benefits): the court rejected the eggshell plaintiff doctrine, holding the Benefits Act does not incorporate the rule that a pre-existing condition cannot be used to reduce the benefit.
However, we disagree that the Benefits Act can be read to incorporate the eggshell principle identified by Ms. Afolayan.
10963: Tucker Act money-mandating jurisdiction over breach of trust duties to tribe under CRP statute and regulations; court held no substantive source of law creates fiduciary duties, so no jurisdiction
We conclude that Ms. Gilham has failed to "identify a substantive source of law that establishes specific fiduciary or other duties."
10986: Illegal exaction claim based on USPTO fee collection dismissed for lack of jurisdiction and failure to state a claim.
we agree with the trial court that it lacks jurisdiction to hear the claim and that Mr. Perry failed to state a claim upon which relief may be granted.
11174: Compensability of destroyed crops as direct takings damages rather than consequential damages; trial court's exclusion of crop losses vacated and remanded for calculation of mature and immature crop values.
It was erroneous to exclude crop damages occurring between 2007 and 2014 from the damages calculation.
11352: Breach-of-contract (Tucker Act money claim): no contract formed between the Tribe and the government; BIA approval of the tribal resolution and construction of Building 2001 were ministerial or sovereign acts lacking mutuality of intent.
we agree with the Claims Court that, on this record, the Tribe failed to establish that it had formed a contract with the government that could be a basis for its breach-of-contract claim
11353: Breach-of-trust claim under the Fort Laramie Treaty and Oahe Act: no substantive source of law imposes a duty to maintain and repair Building 2001.
neither the Treaty of Fort Laramie nor the Oahe Act imposes a trust duty on the United States to maintain and repair Building 2001
11361: Liability under the 1868 Ute Treaty: the Murray Family failed to prove by a preponderance that Officer Norton shot Mr. Murray; the Claims Court's no-liability finding was not clearly erroneous.
we conclude that the Claims Court did not clearly err in finding that the Murray Family failed to establish by a preponderance of the evidence that Officer Norton shot Mr. Murray.
11608: Breach-of-contract claim by former federal employee: the Claims Court properly found no contract existed between Britt and the government, so the money claim failed for the government.

The undisputed facts establish that no pertinent contract existed between Mr. Britt and the government, and the Claims Court properly dismissed Mr. Britt's breach-of-contract claim for lack of subject-matter jurisdiction.
11736: Illegal exaction claim seeking reimbursement of amounts already collected as overpayment debt; the court held the complaint did not plausibly allege an unlawful exaction and affirmed dismissal.
This is not a claim that the government unlawfully exacted money from Mr. Brandenburg.
11993: Tucker Act money claim based on an alleged implied contract and fiduciary duties arising from Social Security number issuance; the court held no contract or fiduciary relationship with the United States was plausibly alleged.
Accordingly, dismissal of Mr. Gorrio's contractual claims was proper.
12091: Other money claims: illegal exaction claim under Norman failed because the statute does not require return of money unlawfully exacted.
Therefore, we agree with the Court of Federal Claims that the Bennetts "fail to allege facts sufficient to establish the Court's illegal exaction jurisdiction."
12097: Other Tucker Act money claim: whether treaties and statutes (Major Crimes Act, ICRA, 1832/1866 treaties) are money-mandating so as to confer Tucker Act jurisdiction over claim for damages from state incarceration; court held no jurisdiction

Because Mr. Scott's claim does not fall within the reach of the Tucker Act, we agree with the Claims Court that it lacked jurisdiction to address his demand for damages from the United States attributable to his prosecution and incarceration by the State of Oklahoma.
12142: Breach of employment agreement: whether the government could recover relocation expenses under the agreement and 5 U.S.C. 5724(i) after the employee failed to complete the twelve-month service requirement; summary judgment for the government on Count I.
We affirm the CFC's grant of summary judgment on Count I of Mr. Auld's complaint because the undisputed facts support the finding that the Government did not breach the Employment Agreement.
12232: Other Tucker Act money claim: whether plaintiff plausibly alleged a bailment contract (voluntary delivery and mutuality) and the consideration required for an implied-in-fact contract with the government; claim dismissed.
Mr. Shaheed does not plausibly allege that he “deliver[ed] personalty” to BOP because BOP seized Mr. Shaheed’s files upon delivery to FCI Berlin.
12384: Equal Pay Act claim for overtime pay: prima facie case (equal work, similar working conditions) not shown, and the government's affirmative defense (differential based on other factor, statutory overtime schemes) sustained

Because we agree with the Claims Court that Ms. Blackwell did not raise a genuine dispute of material fact as to her prima facie case and, in any event, the government successfully raised its affirmative defense, we affirm.
12642: Whether Count Three (breach of trust over water rights) identified a money-mandating source of law under the Tucker Act and Indian Tucker Act; Navajo Nation and Arizona v. Navajo Nation found no duty, so dismissal was affirmed
We affirm the Claims Court's dismissal of Count Three.
12951: Illegal exaction claim to recover H-1B enhanced fees paid on change of status petitions; court held the Enhanced Fee Statutes authorize collection of the fee on change of status petitions, so the exaction claim fails.

We therefore find the Enhanced Fee Statutes authorize USCIS to collect the enhanced fees from employers filing change of status petitions on behalf of their nonimmigrant employees already inside the United States under another status.
12998: Other money claims: whether the RRF statute's 'in addition to amounts otherwise available' and $28.6 billion language caps the Government's liability. The court held there is no clear statutory cap and the obligation attached when applications were received.
the statute's ambiguous appropriations language does not defeat this obligation.
13062: Illegal exaction claim based on IRS accrual of underpayment interest after the 6603 deposit, including the IRS's discretion not to apply successor trusts' deposits to original trusts' liabilities
we are not prepared to hold that the IRS's exercise of its discretion was abusive.
13232: Damages for destroyed structures and personal property (separate property interest from flowage easement) awarded to plaintiffs; affirmed.
The Court of Federal Claims applied our precedent by awarding damages both for the value of the flowage easement and the value of destroyed structures and personal property.
13233: Leasehold advantage damages awarded to Mr. Holland; affirmed.
Thus, the Court of Federal Claims did not err by awarding Mr. Holland compensation.
13234: Lost rent, lost income and utility payments awarded to Mr. Sidhu as landlord; vacated because they are lost business profits tied to use of the easement property.
Accordingly, we hold that the Court of Federal Claims erred by awarding Mr. Sidhu compensation for lost rent and for utility payments.
13235: Displacement and temporary alternative housing costs awarded to several plaintiffs; vacated because the flowage easement already compensates the temporary occupation.
Thus, the Court of Federal Claims erred by awarding Plaintiffs costs for their temporary displacement.
13236: Valuation at zero of the flowage easement on Ms. Popovici's property; vacated and remanded as clear error.
we hold that it was clear error to value the government's permanent right to flood Ms. Popovici's property at $0.
13237: Offset of FEMA emergency relief against plaintiffs' compensation to prevent double recovery; offset affirmed.
We reject Cross-Appellants' argument that the Court of Federal Claims erred by offsetting their compensation awards by the amount already received from FEMA
13439: Copyright infringement damages under 28 U.S.C. §1498(b): the court affirmed a $154,400 award measured by a hypothetical-negotiation license based on actual usage, rejecting the claimant's per-copy measure of $85,913,400.
the trial court's rejection of a per-copy approach based on the record developed in this case is not clearly erroneous.
13461: Salary claims for locality pay and COLA under FEPCA and the Non-Foreign AREA Act: the court held the statutes, even with challenged provisions disregarded, are not money-mandating as to plaintiffs, so no Tucker Act money claim lies.
Here, the statutes upon which Plaintiffs rely, even without the challenged provisions, are not money-mandating as to Plaintiffs.
13962: Whether the Kania exception to Tucker Act contract jurisdiction (sovereign-capacity/criminal-proceeding agreements) bars the breach-of-contract money claim; the court held the exception inapplicable.
The Kania exception to the strong presumption of Tucker Act availability is therefore inapplicable.
13984: Tucker Act money claim for refund of criminal fine, restitution, forfeiture and assessment payments after a presidential pardon; the court found no implied contract, no illegal exaction, and no money-mandating source, so the claim fails for the government.
Mr. Boultbee does not establish the elements required for an implied contract.
14082: Copyright infringement damages under 28 U.S.C. 1498(b): court held a hypothetical negotiation may be used instead of directly applying the licensing agreement's SEWP or License rates; no per se rule requires adopting license rates
Neither statute nor case law requires automatic adoption of royalty rates set out in licensing agreements when calculating infringement damages.
14083: Book of wisdom: trial court legally erred by constructing the hypothetical negotiation with knowledge of the government's later cancellation of TETRA, which tainted the bargaining-position analysis; judgment vacated and remanded
the trial court's construction of the hypothetical negotiation with knowledge of TETRA's future cancellation amounts to legal error in its application of the book of wisdom.
14084: Consideration of the availability of Rhapsody, a similar cheaper software, as weakening claimant's bargaining position in the hypothetical negotiation
the trial court is within its discretion to consider the availability of similar, even if not coextensive, software products.
14085: Willful-infringement statutory damages (increased damages equivalent to 150,000 under 17 U.S.C. 504(c)) are noncompensatory and not recoverable against the government under 1498(b); remanded for determination of any per-seat Studio license
the trial court's grant of increased statutory damages for willful infringement is legal error.
14086: Compensation for unused Studio copies: trial court did not err in assigning unused copies no value because copyright damages need not be per-copy
[t]he law does not require that every award of copyright damages be on a per-copy basis.
14087: Factual findings that the parties would have negotiated development licenses rather than production licenses and a volume discount for development licenses, reviewed for clear error
we see no clear error in the trial court's determination.
14178: Post-judgment interest on Woodley's three reimbursed expenses barred by the no-interest rule absent an explicit waiver of sovereign immunity for interest
we agree with the Court of Federal Claims that the no-interest rule bars recovery of post-judgment interest on Denise Woodley's three expenses.
14179: Post-judgment interest on attorney's fees awarded to counsel jointly hired by the Woodleys denied because neither the URA nor 28 U.S.C. § 1961(c) waives interest immunity
neither the URA nor 28 U.S.C. § 1961(c) waives the government's post-judgment interest immunity
14295: Whether the complaint plausibly states a claim for statutory indemnification under PAA-amended AEA section 170(d) for public liability; court held Cotter is a person indemnified and the liability arises out of or in connection with the contractual activity.
we conclude that Cotter is a “person indemnified” seeking indemnity for a “public liability.”
14412: Other money claims under the Tucker Act: ADA and Rehabilitation Act are not money-mandating sources, and WIOA creates no right to money damages.
But neither statute is money mandating under the Tucker Act because they do not “mandat[e] compensation by the Federal Government for the damages sustained.”
14567: Other money claims under the Tucker Act: the Fourteenth Amendment and other constitutional provisions cited were held not money-mandating, and the 28 U.S.C. § 1495 wrongful-imprisonment claim failed because no imprisonment by the United States was pleaded.
Here, Mr. Bass fails to identify a separate source of law that creates the right to money damages for his claims.
14667: Tribal trust claims based on the Winters doctrine and the 1899 Act: no specific trust duty to construct new infrastructure or secure new water, so no Indian Tucker Act jurisdiction; dismissal affirmed.
We agree with the Claims Court that Winters and the 1899 Act do not impose these trust duties and conclude that the Claims Court properly dismissed these claims.
14668: Tribal trust claims based on the 1906 Act: the Act imposes a trust duty to maintain and operate existing irrigation infrastructure, so the dismissal of those infrastructure claims is vacated and remanded.
The 1906 Act, by its plain text, establishes that the United States accepted a duty to h[o]ld and operate[] the described irrigation systems in trust for the Indians.
14671: Midview Exchange Agreement claim 11 as to water infrastructure is barred by the 2012 settlement agreement release; dismissal affirmed.
We affirm the dismissal of claim 11 insofar as it concerned infrastructure.
14672: Midview Exchange Agreement claim 11 as to water rights: the 2012 settlement exception for water rights may apply, so dismissal is vacated and remanded.
We vacate the Claims Court's dismissal of claim 11 and remand for consideration of these issues.
14687: Other money claims: whether a due process challenge to the § 4208 bar can support Tucker Act jurisdiction absent an illegal exaction.
We thus affirm the dismissal of Ms. Jacobson's complaint by the Court of Federal Claims.
15305: Whether 31 U.S.C. § 5323 is a money-mandating statute supporting Tucker Act jurisdiction over a whistleblower award claim; the court agreed with the Claims Court that it is.
We agree with the Claims Court that 31 U.S.C. § 5323 is a money-mandating statute.
